style_when: the story is about change after hours — automation displacing shifts, a market open all night, capacity running while people sleep
prompt: Architectural photograph at blue hour. Wide asymmetrical framing with the subject anchoring the right third. A sleek, high-end residential wall battery and heavy electrical service panel mounted on the textured exterior wall of a modern dark garage. Deep blue ambient twilight contrasts with the warm amber indicator lights glowing from the battery unit. Thick, industrial-grade conduit runs down the wall, disappearing into the dark driveway below. Crisp architectural lines, 35mm wide lens, long-exposure calm, no moving figures, sophisticated editorial lighting emphasizing the expensive hardware acting as a structural gatekeeper.
negative_prompt: text, typography, letters, numbers, watermark, signage, UI, logos, brands, people, faces, hands
rationale: Architectural night photography perfectly captures the residential infrastructure environment. The blue-hour dusk setting emphasizes the time when home backup is critical, while the illuminated wall hardware highlights the expensive 'gatekeeper' required to unlock the home's power.
subject: a glowing, high-end residential wall battery and heavy electrical service panel mounted on a dark modern garage exterior
core_thesis: Tesla's EVs can now power a home, but this capability is locked behind the steep purchase of an $8,200 wall battery, acting as an expensive gatekeeper.
core_conflict: Abundant vehicle battery capacity vs. steep financial hardware barriers to unlock it.
alt_text: A glowing wall-mounted residential battery and electrical panel on a dark garage exterior at dusk.
caption: The massive potential of vehicle-to-home backup is currently gated by expensive hardware requirements.
title: Home Battery Gatekeeper
